He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV Runnin' Rebels]] and earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC) as a sophomore in 2016.{{cite web|title=Patrick McCaw Bio|url=http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/patrick_mccaw_906699.html|website=UNLVRebels.com|access-date=June 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160628160542/http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/patrick_mccaw_906699.html|archive-date=June 28, 2016|url-status=dead}} McCaw was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the second round of the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He won three [[NBA championship]]s in his first three seasons: two with the [[Golden State Warriors]] and one with the [[Toronto Raptors]], the first [[NBA]] player to do so while switching teams. ==Early life== McCaw was born in [[St. Louis]], Missouri, to Jeffery and Teresa McCaw. He initially attended [[Christian Brothers College High School]] but transferred to [[Montrose Christian School]] as a senior, where McCaw averaged 13 points per game and led the team to a 20–5 record and the National Christian School Athletic Association Division I title. After he graduated, McCaw was ranked as the 38th-best [[shooting guard]] in the country.{{cite web |title=Pat McCaw recruiting profile |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/186687 |access-date=December 29, 2016 |work=ESPN.com}} ==College career== McCaw attended [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]] where, in two seasons, he averaged 12.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 2.0 steals and 31.7 minutes in 65 games. In his sophomore season, McCaw played 33 games and averaged 14.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.45 steals in 33.7 minutes, having the second-most steals in the nation. He earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Mountain West Conference|MWC]] and also was named to their all-defensive team.{{cite web |last=Witt |first=Brian |date=June 23, 2016 |title=Warriors Select Vanderbilt Center Damian Jones With 30th Overall Pick in 2016 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-select-vanderbilt-center-damian-jones-30th-overall-pick-2016-nba-draft |access-date=May 8, 2025 |work=NBA.com}} On April 4, 2016, McCaw declared for the [[2016 NBA draft|NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Grimala|url=http://runrebs.com/2016/04/04/patrick-mccaw-declares-nba-draft/|title=Patrick McCaw Declares for NBA Draft|work=RunRebs.com|date=April 4, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330045406/http://runrebs.com/2016/04/04/patrick-mccaw-declares-nba-draft|archive-date=March 30, 2017|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2016–2018)=== ==== Rookie year and first ring (2016–2017) ==== [[File:Patrick McCaw.jpg|thumb|McCaw during the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]|left]] On June 23, 2016, McCaw was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 38th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He was later traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] on draft night for cash considerations. Warriors executive board member, [[Jerry West]], felt McCaw should not have slipped that far, saying: "People are gonna be sorry they didn't draft him."{{cite web | title=Jerry West: ‘People are gonna be sorry they didn't draft' McCaw | website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California | date=2016-07-13 | url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/jerry-west-people-are-gonna-be-sorry-they-didnt-draft-mccaw/1353271/ | access-date=2025-06-02}} On July 6, 2016, McCaw signed with the Warriors and joined them for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Fahey |first=Andy |date=July 6, 2016 |title=Warriors Sign Rookie Guard Patrick McCaw to Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-mccaw-20160706 |access-date=May 8, 2025 |work=NBA.com}} McCaw made his debut for the Warriors in their season-opener on October 25, 2016, against the [[2016–17 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]]. In nine minutes off the bench, McCaw recorded two points, two assists, a steal and a block in the 129–100 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899377|title=Spurs vs. Warriors – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} On December 8, he scored a then-career-high 10 points, all in the first half of the Warriors' 106–99 victory over the [[2016–17 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2016 |title=Curry scores 26, Warriors beat Jazz 106-99 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899777 |access-date=December 9, 2016 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On December 29, McCaw was assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], Golden State's [[D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-assign-jones-mccaw-santa-cruz-20161229|title=Warriors Assign Damian Jones and Patrick McCaw to Santa Cruz|work=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2016}} The next day, he was recalled by Golden State.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-recall-jones-mccaw-santa-cruz-20161230|title=Warriors Recall Damian Jones and Patrick McCaw from Santa Cruz|work=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2017}} On January 10, 2017, McCaw made his first career start in place of an ill [[Klay Thompson]], contributing a three-pointer in a 107–95 victory over the [[2016–17 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899999|title=Curry, Durant lead Warriors past Heat 107-95|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2017|access-date=January 10, 2017}} McCaw was reassigned to Santa Cruz on January 13,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-assign-looney-mccaw-santa-cruz-20170113|title=Warriors Assign Kevon Looney and Patrick McCaw to Santa Cruz|work=NBA.com|date=January 13, 2017|access-date=January 13, 2017}} and was recalled the next day.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-recall-looney-mccaw-santa-cruz-20170113|title=Warriors Recall Kevon Looney and Patrick McCaw from Santa Cruz|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2017}} On February 13, McCaw made another start in place of Thompson and went on to score a career-high 19 points in a 132–110 loss to the [[2016–17 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |last=Haynes |first=Chris |date=February 13, 2017 |title=Nuggets stun Warriors with record-tying 3-point barrage |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/golden-state-warriors/post/_/id/3740 |access-date=February 16, 2017 |work=ESPN.com}} After starting forward [[Kevin Durant]] suffered a left knee injury on February 28, McCaw started in place of Durant in most games.{{Cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/2017/03/17/patrick-mccaw-gaining-needed-experience-in-kevin-durants-absence/|title=Patrick McCaw gaining needed experience in Kevin Durant's absence|last=Slater|first=Anthony|website=Mercury News|date=March 18, 2017 |access-date=April 20, 2017}} McCaw made his first career playoff start in game 2 of the first round on April 19 in place of injured Durant, which the Warriors won 110–81 over the [[2016–17 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]]. McCaw finished with nine points, five rebounds, a block, a steal and an overall [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus-27]].{{Cite web |last=Steward |first=Carl |date=April 20, 2017 |title=Warriors rookie Patrick McCaw steps up in a pinch for Kevin Durant |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2017/04/19/rookie-patrick-mccaw-steps-up-at-both-ends-and-even-throws-in-a-brief-bit-of-emotion/ |access-date=May 8, 2025 |website=mercurynews.com}} He started in place of Durant again in game 3, contributing eight points, five rebounds, five assists, a block and three steals in a 119–113 comeback victory in Portland.{{Cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/2017/04/23/five-observations-from-the-warriors-game-3-win-in-portland/|title=Five observations from the Warriors' Game 3 win in Portland|last=Slater|first=Anthony|date=April 24, 2017|website=Mercury News|access-date=May 18, 2017}} In game 2 of the Western Conference Finals against the San Antonio Spurs on May 16, McCaw had 18 points, five assists, three rebounds and three steals off the bench to help the Warriors win 136–100. He was 6-for-8 from the field, including 3-for-4 on three-pointers.{{Cite news|url=http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-McCaw-does-best-Iguodala-imitation-in-11151700.php|title=Warriors' McCaw does best Iguodala imitation in Game 2 win|work=SFGate|access-date=May 18, 2017}} McCaw became the first rookie in the NBA with at least 18 points off the bench in a playoff game since [[James Harden]] in 2010, and the first Warriors rookie to do so since [[Robert Parish]] in 1977.{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/third-round-takeaways-20170517|title=Takeaways After Two Games of the Conference Finals|date=May 17, 2017|work=Golden State Warriors|access-date=May 18, 2017}} Six days later, McCaw started in game 4, finishing with six points, four rebounds, two assists, a block and a plus-12 in the close-out 129–115 victory.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400953594|title=Warriors vs. Spurs - Box Score - May 22, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 23, 2017}} The Warriors went on to win the [[2017 NBA Finals]] after defeating the [[2016–17 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] in five games. The Warriors finished the playoffs with a 16–1 record, the best postseason winning percentage in NBA history.{{cite web |date=June 14, 2017 |title=Warriors (16–1) Record Best Postseason Winning Percentage in NBA History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2715556-warriors-16-1-record-best-postseason-winning-percentage-in-nba-history |access-date=May 8, 2025 |website=Bleacher Report}} ==== Second championship (2017–2018) ==== On November 27, 2017, McCaw, starting in place of an injured [[Stephen Curry]], scored a season-best 16 points with career highs of seven assists and four steals in a 110–106 loss to the [[2017–18 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975047|title=Curry, Durant sit out as Kings beat Warriors 110-106|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2017|access-date=November 28, 2017}} On March 31, 2018, McCaw left late in the third quarter of the Warriors' 112–96 victory over the Kings after a scary landing following an undercut by [[Vince Carter]]. McCaw drove the baseline and went down with a thud with 41.8 seconds left in the quarter and was hit in the lower body by Carter. McCaw laid still on the floor for roughly 10 minutes before being stretchered off and taken to [[UC Davis Medical Center]] for further evaluation.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975888|title=Warriors' McCaw injured in scary fall as team beats Kings|work=ESPN.com|date=March 31, 2018|access-date=April 1, 2018}} The following day, he was released from the hospital with a bruised lumbar spine.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975899|title=Warriors shake off rough start and roll past Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2018|access-date=April 1, 2018}} McCaw returned from injury in game 6 of the Western Conference Finals against the [[2017–18 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]] on May 26.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401032766|title=Klay Thompson score 35, Warriors force Game 7 in West finals|work=ESPN.com|date=May 26, 2018|access-date=May 26, 2018}} The Warriors went on to defeat the Rockets in game 7 two days later to advance to the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the fourth straight season, where they won their second straight championship with a four-game sweep of the Cavaliers. Following the 2017–18 season, McCaw became a [[restricted free agent]]. In October 2018, he allowed the Warriors' $1.71 million qualifying offer to expire without accepting it,{{cite web|last=Slater|first=Anthony|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/563341/2018/10/02/trying-to-make-sense-of-patrick-mccaws-hardball-tactics-with-the-warriors/|title=Trying to make sense of Patrick McCaw's hardball tactics with the Warriors|work=The Athletic|date=October 2, 2018|access-date=October 13, 2018|url-access=subscription }}{{cite web|last=Adams|first=Luke|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/10/latest-on-patrick-mccaw.html|title=Latest On Patrick McCaw|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 3, 2018|access-date=October 13, 2018}} and reportedly declined another two-year, $5.2 million offer from the team.{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Sources: Cavs to sign Patrick McCaw to two-year, $6M offer sheet |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25632943 |access-date=December 28, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} McCaw remained restricted, with the Warriors retaining the right to match any offer from another team. ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2019)=== After remaining on the free agent market for nearly six months, McCaw signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on December 30, 2018. The Warriors had declined to match the offer,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/12/30/report-warriors-wont-match-cavaliers-offer-sheet-patrick-mccaw|title=Report: Warriors decline to match Cavaliers' offer sheet for Patrick McCaw|work=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2018|access-date=December 31, 2018}} which was reportedly a non-guaranteed, two-year, $6 million deal.{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Cavaliers Sign Patrick McCaw |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mccaw-signing-181228 |access-date=December 29, 2018 |work=NBA.com}} On January 6, 2019, McCaw was waived by the Cavaliers after appearing in three games.{{Cite web |last=Fedor |first=Chris |date=2019-01-07 |title=Cleveland Cavaliers sign Cameron Payne to 10-day contract |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2019/01/cleveland_cavaliers_sign_camer.html |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=cleveland.com |language=en}}{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=January 6, 2019 |title=Cavaliers waive Patrick McCaw after acquiring guard last week |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25700179 |access-date=January 6, 2019 |work=ESPN.com}} ===Toronto Raptors (2019–2021)=== On January 10, 2019, McCaw signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |last=Naje |first=B. |date=January 10, 2019 |title=Raptors Sign Patrick McCaw |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-patrick-mccaw |access-date=January 10, 2019 |work=NBA.com}} The Raptors advanced to the [[2019 NBA Finals]] against McCaw's former team, the Golden State Warriors, where they won the series in six games to give McCaw his third straight championship. McCaw became the third player ever to win titles in three consecutive seasons with different teams, joining [[Steve Kerr]] and [[Frank Saul (basketball)|Frank Saul]],{{cite web|last=Palermo|first=Gregg|url=https://fox2now.com/2019/06/13/st-louis-native-patrick-mccaw-wins-nba-championship-with-toronto-raptors/|title=St. Louis native Patrick McCaw wins NBA Championship with Toronto Raptors|work=fox2now.com|date=June 13, 2019|access-date=June 13, 2019}} and McCaw became the first player to win three consecutive NBA titles since [[Shaquille O'Neal]], [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Robert Horry]], [[Derek Fisher]], [[Rick Fox]], [[Brian Shaw (basketball)|Brian Shaw]] and [[Devean George]] led the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to three straight wins from 2000 to 2002.{{cite web|last=Srinivasan|first=Arun|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/raptors-patrick-mccaw-becomes-first-player-to-3-peat-since-shaq-kobe-040903497.html|title=Raptors' McCaw becomes first player to 3-peat since Shaq and Kobe's Lakers|work=Yahoo.com|date=June 13, 2019|access-date=June 13, 2019}} McCaw also became the seventh player to win a championship during each of his first three years in the league.{{Cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2019/6/14/18679322/patrick-mccaw-threepeat-toronto-raptors-golden-state-warriors|title=Three-Pat: How Patrick McCaw Made History In the 2019 NBA Finals|last=Sherman|first=Rodger|date=2019-06-14|website=The Ringer|access-date=2019-06-14}} On July 8, 2019, the Raptors announced that they had re-signed with McCaw.{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=July 8, 2019 |title=Raptors Re-Sign Patrick McCaw |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-re-sign-patrick-mccaw |access-date=July 8, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} On November 6, it was announced that McCaw had undergone arthroscopic surgery on his left knee and was expected to be sidelined for about four weeks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/mccaw-injury-update|title=McCaw Injury Update|date=November 6, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 6, 2019}} On April 9, 2021, the Raptors waived McCaw.{{Cite tweet|number=1380521899193737219|user=Raptors|title=Thank you for everything, Champ.
